properties.location: the Upper Murray and Mitta Mitta Rivers
properties.webBody:
This Flood Watch is being issued for the Upper Murray and Mitta Mitta Rivers.

Renewed river level rises are expected and minor flooding may develop across the flood watch area from Tuesday. Some isolated moderate flooding is also possible.

Moderate rainfall has been forecast for the flood watch area from overnight Monday through to Wednesday morning.

Renewed river level rises are expected across the flood watch area with minor flooding possible from Tuesday. Isolated moderate flooding may also develop if the rainfall is in the upper end of the forecast range.

Catchments across the flood watch area are wet and stream levels remain elevated as a result of recent rainfall and flooding is still ongoing in some catchments. Stream levels are likely to respond quickly to forecast rainfall.

Catchments likely to be affected include:
  • Upper Murray and Mitta Mitta Rivers
  • Kiewa River
  • Ovens and King Rivers
  • Broken River
  • Seven and Castle Creeks
  • Goulburn River Eildon to Seymour
  • Goulburn River downstream of Seymour
  • Loddon River
  • Avoca River
Flood Warnings are current for the following catchments: Kiewa, Loddon and Avoca.

This flood watch is for communities in Victoria. Floods have different impacts on either side of the Murray River. For information and warnings relevant to NSW, visit www.hazardwatch.gov.au. Always follow advice from your State’s emergency services

Stay informed - monitor your local conditions and remain alert.
What you should do:
  • Decide what you and your family will do if flooding impacts you. For information on how to prepare go to www.ses.vic.gov.au/get-ready/floodsafe.
  • Stay informed by listening to emergency broadcasters and monitoring warnings.
  • Farmers should consider moving livestock and machinery to higher ground.
  • Monitor weather forecasts and river levels. Go to www.bom.gov.au/vic/warnings/
Impacts in your area: 
  • Caravan parks and camping grounds may be flooded.
  • Areas around rivers and streams may be flooded.
This message was issued by State Emergency Service.

The next update is expected by 24/08/2026 03:00 pm or as the situation changes.

Use multiple sources to stay informed:
  • www.emergency.vic.gov.au
  • VicEmergency Hotline - freecall 1800 226 226
  • VicEmergency app
  • Facebook
  • Tune in to ABC Local Radio, commercial and designated community radio stations, or News24 TV.
Accessibility:
The following services can help you, or someone you know, access information during an emergency.
  • To access this information in other languages, call the Translating and Interpreting Service on 131 450 (freecall) and ask them to call VicEmergency Hotline.
  • If you are deaf, hard of hearing, or have a speech/communication impairment, contact the National Relay Service and ask them to call the VicEmergency Hotline.

properties.location: Murray River downstream of Tocumwal to Barham
properties.webBody:
This Minor Flood Warning is being issued for the Murray River downstream of Tocumwal to Barham.

  • Upstream flows from the Murray River, combined with flood waters from the Goulburn River, are causing minor flooding along the Murray River at Barham.
  • The Murray River at Barham is currently at 5.51m and steady, just above the minor flood level (5.50m).
  • River levels are expected to remain around the minor flood level through to the end of the coming week as flood waters continue to arrive from upstream.
  •  The Murray River at Barham may reach around 5.60m during Wednesday 26 August, with minor flooding.
Stay informed - monitor your local conditions and remain alert.
What you should do: 
  • Be prepared to act if your situation changes.
  • Stay informed by listening to emergency broadcasters and monitoring warnings. 
  • Floodwater is dangerous - never drive, walk or ride through floodwater. 
  • Monitor weather forecasts and river levels. Go to www.bom.gov.au/vic/warnings/
Impacts in your area: 
  • High river levels and potential flooding in areas close to rivers and streams.
  • Camping grounds may be flooded.
  • Boating in floodwaters is dangerous due to debris, submerged trees and other hidden dangers.
This message was issued by State Emergency Service.

The next update is expected by 24/08/2026 01:30 pm or as the situation changes.

Use multiple sources to stay informed:
  • www.emergency.vic.gov.au
  • VicEmergency Hotline - freecall 1800 226 226

properties.location: Loddon River Loddon Weir to Kerang
properties.webBody:
This Minor Flood Warning is being issued for the Loddon River Loddon Weir to Kerang.

  • Rainfall early last week resulted in a second flood peak that is now downstream of Loddon Weir and moving towards Appin South.
  • At 11am on Sunday, the Loddon River at Loddon Weir was at 5.89m and falling, above the minor flood level (3.30m).
  • The Loddon River at Appin South is currently at 2.56m and steady, below the minor flood level (2.80m).
  • Renewed river level rises are likely at Appin South during Sunday, with renewed minor flooding likely from Monday as the second flood peak arrives.
  • Forecast rainfall early next week may cause renewed river level rises across the Loddon River catchment.
Stay informed - monitor your local conditions and be prepared to act if your situation changes.
What you should do: 
  • Be prepared to act if your situation changes.
  • Drivers must be alert to water over roads, especially overnight when visibility is poor.
  • Do not enter flooded areas. Turn around and find a safe alternative route.
  • Never drive, walk or ride through floodwater.
  • Be aware of road hazards including mud, debris and damaged roads or bridges.
Impacts in your area: 
  • High river levels and potential flooding in areas close to rivers and streams.
  • Over-floor flooding of dwellings is not currently expected.
  • Impacts expected to be limited to inundation of lower areas of Loddon floodplain with possible inundation of some minor local roads.
  • Roads and bridges may be closed due to flooding.
  • Boating in floodwaters is dangerous due to debris, submerged trees and other hidden dangers.
This message was issued by State Emergency Service.

The next update is expected by 24/08/2026 01:00 pm or as the situation changes.

properties.webBody:
This Moderate Flood Warning is being issued for the Avoca River downstream of Charlton Town.

  • Rainfall early last week resulted in the Avoca River at Charlton Town reaching a peak just below the moderate flood level on Saturday night.
  • At 10am on Sunday, the Avoca River downstream of Charlton Town was at 5.49m and falling, above the moderate flood level (5.00m).
  • Downstream at Quambatook, river levels are expected to rise again as upstream flows arrive; however, levels are expected to remain below the minor flood level through Sunday and into Monday.
  • Forecast rainfall early next week may cause renewed river level rises across the Avoca River catchment.
Stay informed - monitor your local conditions and be prepared to act if your situation changes.
What you should do: 
  • Be prepared to act if your situation changes.
  • Drivers must be alert to water over roads, especially overnight when visibility is poor.
  • Do not enter flooded areas. Turn around and find a safe alternative route.
  • Never drive, walk or ride through floodwater.
  • Be aware of road hazards including mud, debris and damaged roads or bridges.
Impacts in your area: 
  • Many local roads are closed or have speed restrictions. Drivers must follow diversions. For more information on road closures visit the VicTraffic website.
  • Flooding of farmland downstream of Glenloth around Bunguluke and Ninyeunook, and inundation of local roads such as Jeruk River Road North and Ninyeunook Road.
  • Floodwaters may persist for several days as they move through the floodplain.
  • High river levels and potential flooding in areas close to rivers and streams.
This message was issued by State Emergency Service.

properties.webBody:
This Minor Flood Warning is being issued for the Avoca River to Charlton Town.

  • Rainfall early last week resulted in the Avoca River at Charlton Town reaching a peak at 5.86m around 9.30pm Saturday, just below the moderate flood level (5.90m).
  • The Avoca River at Charlton Town is currently at 5.33m and falling, and is expected to remain above the minor flood level (4.00m) through Sunday and into Monday.
  • Downstream at Quambatook, river levels are expected to rise again as upstream flows arrive; however, levels are expected to remain below the minor flood level through Sunday and into Monday.
  • Forecast rainfall early next week may cause renewed river level rises across the Avoca River catchment.
Stay informed - monitor your local conditions and remain alert.
What you should do: 
  • Drivers must be alert to water over roads, especially overnight when visibility is poor.
  • Do not enter flooded areas. Turn around and find a safe alternative route.
  • Never drive, walk or ride through floodwater.
  • Be aware of road hazards including mud, debris and damaged roads or bridges.
Impacts in your area: 
  • Many local roads are closed or have speed restrictions. Drivers must follow diversions. For more information on road closures visit the VicTraffic website.
  • Flooding of farmland downstream of Glenloth around Bunguluke and Ninyeunook, and inundation of local roads such as Jeruk River Road North and Ninyeunook Road.
  • Floodwaters may persist for several days as they move through the floodplain.
  • High river levels and potential flooding in areas close to rivers and streams.
This message was issued by State Emergency Service.

The next update is expected by 24/08/2026 12:00 pm or as the situation changes.
